issues.description: Seen.ref and Seen.parent complect three distinct concerns into one mutable record
issues.detail: ref means 'inherit JSON from this', parent means 'clone source', and ref=null means 'already flattened'. Three different facts about three different times are stored in two fields on the same place. The flatten code then has to disambiguate via isParentRef = (zod.parent === ref), which is exactly the complecting made visible. Separate the inheritance edge from the clone-lineage edge from the visited flag.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as a value-equality primitive in two hot dedup loops
issues.detail: Two near-identical loops dedup child keys against parent def via JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b). That is place-oriented equality smuggled through string serialization: key-order sensitive, undefined-dropping, NaN/Infinity-lossy, and O(n*size) per schema. The fact you want is structural value equality on JSON Schema fragments; name it, write it once, and use it. Don't ship stringify-equals.

issues.description: flattenRef now mutates the schema object in place across three overlapping phases
issues.detail: Phase 1 merges ref properties, phase 2 deletes parent-only keys, phase 3 may overwrite $ref from a different parent and dedup again. Each phase reads what the previous one wrote on the same place. This is the classic place-oriented trap: behavior depends on traversal order plus prior mutations. A pure (child, refDef, parentDef) -> finalJson function would make the ordering explicit and testable.

issues.description: override callback semantics silently changed; overrideCount doubling from 6 to 12 is asserted, not explained
issues.detail: Previously isParent suppressed override; now override always runs. The test simply updates the magic number from 6 to 12. That is a behavior change to a user-visible extension point with no recorded rationale. Either document why parents must now receive override callbacks (and what users who relied on the old contract should do), or restore the guard. A doubled count is a symptom, not a specification.

issues.description: play.ts repurposed as ad-hoc debug script and imports from source path
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from ./packages/zod/src/index.js and console.logs two cases. That is a scratchpad, not a value the repo should carry. Either delete it, move the investigation into a real test, or keep play.ts as the documented sandbox it was. Mixing the two confuses what the file is for.

issues.description: Seen.ref overloaded with three states (undefined, $ZodType, null) acting as a visited flag
issues.detail: ref: undefined means 'no inheritance', a schema means 'inherit from this', and null means 'already flattened, don't recurse'. That is identity, value, and time pressed into one field. A boolean visited and a separate ref: $ZodType | undefined would name the two facts and make the recursion guard explicit instead of overloading the data slot.

review.summary: The fix works, but it works by piling more place-oriented mutation onto an already complected pipeline. Seen.ref and Seen.parent now carry three different concerns — inheritance source, clone lineage, and visited flag — and flattenRef mutates the schema object across three overlapping phases that depend on each other's writes. JSON.stringify-as-equality appears twice as the dedup primitive; that is a value question dressed up as a string question. The real question that should have been asked first: what is the actual data model of "a JSON schema fragment with an inheritance chain and a clone lineage"? Name those as values, write the merge as a pure function over them, and the override-count-doubled-from-6-to-12 stops being a mystery.
